Chat Edit: 'my entire portfolio website codebase (static HTML/CSS/JS on GitHub Pages). You are operating inside Google Antigravity. Your job is to perform a maximum-depth, production-quality audit across the entire repository and deliver verifiable Artifacts (file evidence, diffs, checklists, and browser-based validation where possible). Antigravity should prioritize trustworthy deliverables, not raw tool logs.

Context

Site: personal portfolio + case studies

Goal: convert executive assistants, operations leaders, founders, hiring managers into “contact / interview me”

Positioning: systems + automation + operations professional

Tech: static HTML/CSS/JS, deployed on GitHub Pages

ZIP includes: all pages, /assets CSS/JS, images/fonts/icons, robots.txt, sitemap.xml, site.webmanifest, security.txt, .htaccess (if present), plus any other config files

Roles (act simultaneously)

Senior Front-End Engineer • Senior UI/UX Designer • Senior Accessibility Specialist (WCAG 2.1 AA) • Senior SEO & Technical Marketing Specialist • Senior Performance Engineer • Senior QA Engineer • Brand & Content Strategist

Hard Rules (non-negotiable)

Do not praise. Treat this as a strict release gate.

Do not ask follow-up questions. If unclear, assume and label assumptions.

Be specific and testable. No generic advice.

Every issue must include:

exact file path(s) + selector/function/snippet

why it matters (user + technical + business impact)

concrete fix (diff/patch style preferred)

verification steps (manual + tooling)

If not provable from the repo alone, label as Hypothesis and provide confirm steps.

Prefer fixes that reduce future drift: shared components/partials, consistent tokens, simpler architecture.

Hosting reality: GitHub Pages may ignore server configs like .htaccess; call out anything that won’t actually apply. (If you cannot confirm hosting behavior from repo alone, mark Hypothesis and include verification.)

REQUIRED ARTIFACTS (you must generate these deliverables)
Artifact A — Repository Inventory Map

Create a concise but complete inventory:

All HTML pages (include case studies)

All CSS files and which pages import them

All JS files and which pages import them

Key assets (images/fonts/icons), including duplicates/near-duplicates

Repeated structures that should be components (header/nav/footer/cards/buttons/tags/case study sections)

Any build tooling or lack thereof (minification/bundling status)

Artifact B — Release Gate Checklist (PASS/WARN/FAIL)

A gatekeeping checklist that covers all pages, with each line item including:

PASS/WARN/FAIL

evidence (file path + snippet/selector)

fix summary (one line)

verification method

Artifact C — Exhaustive Issue Register

A complete issue list. For every issue:

Severity: Blocker / High / Medium / Low

Tags: [FE] [UX] [A11Y] [SEO] [Perf] [QA] [Brand] [Security]

What is wrong (specific + testable)

Why it matters

Exact location (file path + snippet/selector/function)

Concrete fix (diff/patch style)

How to verify (steps + tools)

Artifact D — Page-by-Page Audit

For every HTML page found:

IA/UX friction points

A11y pitfalls (keyboard, focus, landmarks, ARIA, contrast risks)

SEO metadata + structured data notes

internal linking + conversion path

performance bottlenecks

Artifact E — Cross-Cutting Consistency Report

Across the whole site:

design tokens usage consistency (colors/type/spacing/radius/shadow)

component + state consistency (hover/focus/active/disabled)

navigation + footer consistency

content/voice/brand consistency

Artifact F — Core Web Vitals Plan

LCP/INP/CLS risk analysis and specific fixes

render-blocking resources

font strategy

image strategy (formats, responsive images, lazy loading)

third-party scripts strategy
Include realistic target metrics and a step-by-step sequence.

Artifact G — WCAG 2.1 AA Conformance Report

keyboard navigation

focus management

landmark structure

ARIA correctness

contrast risks

prefers-reduced-motion handling
Include a checklist of required changes + how to collect testing evidence.

Artifact H — SEO & Technical Marketing Plan

titles/descriptions/canonicals per page

robots.txt + sitemap.xml correctness and consistency

schema strategy (JSON-LD) with recommended snippets

social preview strategy (OG/Twitter)

keyword + content alignment recommendations for ops/automation audiences

Artifact I — QA Test Plan

smoke tests per page

responsive breakpoint plan (320 / 375–414 / 768–1024 / 1440+)

browser matrix (Chrome, Safari, Firefox, Edge; mobile Safari + Chrome Android)

regression risks and mitigation

Artifact J — Fix-First PR Plan (3–6 PRs)

Group all fixes into 3–6 PRs ordered by impact. Each PR must include:

scope summary

expected files touched

acceptance criteria

test plan

Artifact K — Final Decision Package

Launch readiness score out of 100 with breakdown: A11y / SEO / Perf / UX / Code / Brand / Security

Top 10 leverage improvements remaining

v1.1 feature list aligned to decision-makers

Go/No-Go: “Ready to send to hiring managers? Yes/No” + rationale

HOW TO EXECUTE INSIDE ANTIGRAVITY (do this as part of the work)

Unzip and index the repository (build a project map).

Run static analysis by inspection:

identify duplicate markup patterns (header/footer/etc.)

identify unused selectors/assets (use Coverage-style reasoning if actual coverage isn’t available)

identify brittle selectors, missing null checks, non-deferred scripts

Produce diff-style patches for the highest-impact fixes (at minimum: top Blocker/High issues).

Where feasible, use Antigravity’s browser/testing capabilities to generate evidence artifacts:

Lighthouse runs (Performance/SEO/A11y) with reported findings

keyboard-only navigation recording notes (tab order, focus visibility)

optional axe-based findings (if available)

network waterfall observations for LCP assets
If tooling isn’t available in this environment, label as Hypothesis and provide exact steps to run locally.

Antigravity is expected to produce Artifacts that are inspectable and verifiable (checklists, diffs, summaries, recordings/screenshots).

AUDIT DIMENSIONS (must cover all, across all pages)
1) Global Architecture & Code Quality

project structure, conventions, duplication, dead code

CSS tokens and component patterns

JS gating, modularization, defensive patterns

maintainability and drift risks

2) HTML Semantics & Accessibility (WCAG 2.1 AA)

headings, landmarks, skip link behavior, focus management

interactive semantics and ARIA correctness

keyboard operability and focus-visible styling

contrast risks and reduced-motion

3) CSS, Layout, Responsiveness & Design System

breakpoint behavior; overflow/scroll-x; wrapping issues

spacing and typography scale consistency

component/state consistency and redundant/conflicting CSS

4) JavaScript & Cross-Browser Robustness

console errors risk, race conditions, brittle selectors

performance safety (scroll handlers, long tasks)

graceful degradation, feature detection

filtering logic robustness (if present)

5) Performance & Core Web Vitals

LCP/INP/CLS drivers and exact fixes

images/fonts/render-blocking resources

minification/bundling strategy suitable for static GitHub Pages

6) SEO & Technical Marketing

per-page metadata quality and uniqueness

canonical, OG/Twitter, schema validity and completeness

robots/sitemap correctness

internal linking + conversion funnel strength

7) UX, Interaction Design & Content Strategy

5-second clarity, CTA hierarchy, proof density

case study structure and credibility assets

microcopy improvements aligned to ops/automation hiring intent

8) Security, Privacy & Analytics

external link safety

inline script patterns

CSP/header reality on GH Pages

analytics placement and privacy best practices

OUTPUT ORDER (must follow exactly)

Executive summary (5–10 bullets, highest impact only)

Artifact A — Repository Inventory Map

Artifact B — Release Gate Checklist (PASS/WARN/FAIL)

Artifact C — Exhaustive Issue Register

Artifact D — Page-by-Page Audit

Artifact E — Cross-Cutting Consistency Report

Artifact F — Core Web Vitals Plan

Artifact G — WCAG 2.1 AA Conformance Report

Artifact H — SEO & Technical Marketing Plan

Artifact I — QA Test Plan

Artifact J — Fix-First PR Plan (3–6 PRs)

Artifact K — Final Decision Package

Begin now with the repository inventory, then proceed in order.'
